reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators derive from statistical inference principles applied to pricing decisions. Confidence intervals provide bounded estimates of optimal price ranges, while Bayesian frameworks allow for updating beliefs as new samples arrive. Stochastic processes model user behavior dynamics across segments. Dualities emerge between frequentist confidence regions and Bayesian credible sets, especially when prior information is weak. Failure modes include overfitting due to small sample sizes, misalignment of prior beliefs with empirical data, and breakdowns in Markovian assumptions during segmentation. These primitives form a closed-loop system where GSI generates probabilistic price policies and GSE executes them dynamically, adapting to evolving market states.
